name: Adverbial Smoothing Density
description: Evaluates the density of qualifying adverbs used to forcefully guarantee transition smoothness and assertiveness.
mechanism: To achieve the highly polished, effortlessly flowing prose demanded by user prompts, generative AIs systematically rely on adverbs to lubricate otherwise jarring sentence transitions. Words like 'additionally', 'importantly', 'significantly', and 'arguably' are heavily over-indexed in LLM outputs to simulate a logical bridge where an actual semantic bridge might be weak. Compounding this, LLMs overuse intensifiers ('extremely', 'profoundly', 'deeply') when prompted to be 'emotional' or 'thoughtful', lacking the human capacity to convey emotion purely through subtext or visceral nouns. This method counts the ratio of these specific 'smoothing' adverbs and intensifiers per 100 words compared to an organic human baseline.
parameters:
Analysis: POS Tagging & Vocabulary Indexing
Metric: Transition/Intensifier Adverb Density per 100 Tokens
Output: 0-100 Adverbial Crutch Score
accuracy: Moderate — 60-70%, as it strongly shares overlap with novice human writers attempting to sound academic.
source: Stylometric NLP analysis and corpus linguistics.
useCase: Detecting AI essays, cover letters, and promotional materials that are structurally weak but attempt to sound persuasive and deeply connected via excessive adverb use.
strengths:
• Directly identifies the 'lazy transition' habits of popular LLMs.
• Light footprint relying purely on standard Part-of-Speech (POS) tagging and word lists.
• Highly persistent signature: even minor prompt variations struggle to suppress the model's reliance on adverbs for sentence fluidity.
limitations:
• Low-tier human writers (e.g., struggling students) also heavily abuse adverbs to hit word counts, massively spiking the false positive rate.
• Useless in technical or minimalist genres where adverbs are structurally discouraged for both human and machine.
• Simple to defeat if the prompt explicitly demands the style of Ernest Hemingway (who famously despised adverbs).

references.title: Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
